references.text: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's suffering servant would be "counted among transgressors" ([ref:Jes 53:12|Isaiah 53:12]). This was literally fulfilled when Jesus was crucified between two criminals.
Matthew's parallel account of the crucifixion at Golgotha, where Jesus was crucified between two thieves ([ref:Matt 27:33-38|Matthew 27:33-38]).
Mark's parallel account of the crucifixion, where the place is called Golgotha and Jesus is crucified between two thieves, one on his right and one on his left ([ref:Mark 15:22-27|Mark 15:22-27]).
John's account of the crucifixion, where Jesus carries his cross to the Skull and is crucified with two others, one on each side ([ref:Joh 19:17-18|John 19:17-18]).
Moses set up a bronze snake on a pole so that those who looked at it were healed ([ref:4 Mos 21:8-9|Numbers 21:8-9]). Jesus compared his own exaltation on the cross to this event (cf. John 3:14).

The psalmist describes his sufferings prophetically: "they have pierced my hands and my feet" and "I can count all my bones" ([ref:Sal 22:17-18|Psalms 22:17-18]). This points forward to the sufferings of the crucifixion.

Jesus himself quoted Isaiah 53:12 and said that what was written about him – "he was counted among lawbreakers" – had to be fulfilled ([ref:Luk 22:37|Luke 22:37]). The crucifixion between two criminals was this fulfillment.
The further account of the two criminals who were crucified with Jesus: one mocked him, while the other repented and received a promise of paradise ([ref:Luk 23:39-43|Luke 23:39-43]).

Paul writes that "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" ([ref:Gal 3:13|Galatians 3:13]). The crucifixion was the concrete event where Christ took the curse upon himself.
The law stated that anyone who was hung on a tree was cursed by God ([ref:5 Mos 21:22-23|Deuteronomy 21:22-23]). Jesus' crucifixion fulfilled this curse on behalf of humanity.
Jesus "endured the cross, disregarding its shame" ([ref:Hebr 12:2|Hebrews 12:2]). The place Kranion (Golgotha) became the site where he completed his suffering and entered into his glory.
